ing: frozen, thawed, or use collard greens
st: If using frozen cassava leaves, thaw them. If using collard greens, remove the tough stems and chop the leaves finely.
Put the greens in a large pot with [[2 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 45 minutes until very soft.
Drain the greens and chop or pulse them in a food processor into a coarse paste, as cassava leaves are traditionally pounded.
Heat the palm oil in a clean pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, garlic and bell pepper for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the eggplant and cook for 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the green paste, the remaining [[1 cup]] water, salt and pepper. Stir well.
Mix the peanut butter with a ladle of the hot cooking liquid until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Add the spinach, cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring often to prevent sticking.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve hot with rice, ugali or boiled potatoes.
Soak the wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes so they do not burn.
Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic, salt, pepper and paprika in a large bowl.
Add the meat and toss until coated. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Thread the meat onto skewers, alternating with pieces of onion and bell pepper.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and oil the grates lightly.
Grill the skewers for 10 to 14 minutes, turning every few minutes, until browned all over and cooked through. Goat and beef should reach at least 160°F/71°C.
Rest the skewers for 5 minutes, then serve hot with fries, grilled plantain or a chili sauce.
Bring [[3 cups]] water and the salt to a boil in a heavy saucepan.
In a bowl, whisk [[0.5 cup]] cornmeal with the remaining [[1 cup]] cold water to make a smooth slurry.
Pour the slurry into the boiling water, stirring, and cook for 3 minutes until it forms a thin porridge.
Lower the heat to medium-low. Add the remaining cornmeal a handful at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon after each addition.
Keep stirring and pressing the mixture against the side of the pot for 5 minutes until it pulls away from the pan and is stiff.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 5 minutes to cook the flour through.
Shape into a smooth mound using a wet spoon or bowl. Serve hot with stew or greens, eating with your fingers.
Rub a little oil on your hands, then peel the plantains with a knife by cutting off the ends and slicing down the skin. Cut into chunks and put them in water so they do not darken.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef for 8 minutes, stirring.
Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes, carrot, salt and pepper and cook 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Add [[2 cups]] water, cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until the beef is almost tender.
Drain the plantains and add them to the pot with the remaining [[1 cup]] water so they are nearly covered.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the plantains are soft and the sauce has thickened. Stir gently and add water if it dries out.
Taste and adjust the salt. Sprinkle with cilantro and serve hot.
Drain the soaked beans and rinse well. Put them in a pot with [[4 cups]] fresh water.
Bring to a rolling boil and boil for 10 minutes to destroy natural toxins, then lower the heat and simmer until the beans are nearly tender.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and tomato and cook 3 minutes.
Add the beans with their cooking liquid, the pumpkin, [[1 cup]] water and the salt.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until the pumpkin is soft and the beans are fully tender.
Mash a few pieces of pumpkin against the pot to thicken the stew slightly. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve hot as a side with rice, ugali or boiled potatoes.
Peel the plantains with a knife, cut into chunks and keep them in cold water until needed.
Heat the palm oil in a large pot over medium heat. Brown the beef for 8 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper and garlic and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes, salt and pepper and cook for 5 minutes until saucy.
Add [[2 cups]] water, cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the beef begins to soften.
Drain the plantains and add them with [[1 cup]] more water. Cover and simmer 20 minutes until tender.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 3 minutes until wilted.
Lightly mash some of the plantain into the sauce so it thickens. Taste, adjust the salt and serve hot.

ing: such as whitebait, smelt or small sardines, cleaned
st: Rinse the fish in cold water and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Mix the cornstarch, salt, pepper and chili powder in a shallow dish.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Test with a pinch of flour, which should sizzle at once.
Toss a handful of fish in the seasoned starch, shaking off the extra.
Fry the fish in small batches for 3 minutes until crisp and golden. Do not crowd the pot.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. Repeat with the rest, letting the oil come back to temperature.
Serve hot and crunchy, whole with the heads and tails, with lemon wedges for squeezing.

ing: fresh, such as habanero or Scotch bonnet, stems removed
st: Wear gloves, as these chilies are very hot. Remove the stems and roughly chop the chilies. Keep your hands away from your eyes.
Wash a small glass jar and its lid in hot soapy water and dry it fully.
Put the chilies, garlic and salt in a food processor and pulse into a coarse paste.
Pour the oil into a small saucepan and add the chili paste.
Heat on low, stirring now and then, for 15 minutes. The oil should barely bubble, never smoke.
Turn off the heat and let it cool for 30 minutes.
Pour into the jar, seal and refrigerate. Use only a few drops at a time, and keep for up to 2 weeks.
